security_findings.finding: No length/size cap on plan.steps array before iterating.
security_findings.note: Not wired to any live fetch today; real impact is zero until connected to a network boundary. Cap should be added when wiring happens (tracked in follow-up task).
Confirmed inert by design — properties are only read via dot access, never merged/assigned, so prototype pollution is not possible through this code path.

security_findings.finding: No upper sanity bound on affectedFileCount (e.g. Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER passes).
security_findings.note: Soft hardening item, not exploitable beyond a UI glitch; can be added alongside the size cap when the validator is actually wired to a backend boundary.

security_findings.finding: Error strings are pure structural messages (field name + expected shape), never echo attacker-supplied raw values.
security_findings.note: Confirmed safe to log/display — good practice, preserved as-is.

security_findings.finding: The validator exists but is not yet called anywhere — Saga #262's original finding (PlanCard renders unvalidated backend data) remains technically open in the running application.
security_findings.note: Architectural, not a bug in this task's own scope: there is no real backend/fetch integration point in the codebase yet (same boundary as #264-267). Cannot be 'fixed' without inventing a fake integration point. Follow-up Saga task opened to wire validatePlanResponse into ChatScreen once real backend integration lands, and to tighten PlanCard's PlanStep.operationType type to match KNOWN_OPERATION_TYPES at that point.

approved_points: Fail-closed design confirmed for every malformed shape.
Number edge cases (NaN, Infinity, floats, negatives) correctly rejected via Number.isInteger + >= 0, no coercion used.
No prototype pollution vector — read-only property access.
Duplicate-order detection is O(n), fails fast during iteration.
Files confirmed untracked and match described content exactly; 14 test cases cover AC-1 through AC-8; 96/96 tests + tsc --noEmit clean.
overall_assessment: Validator itself is well-written, fail-closed, free of type-coercion/prototype-pollution risk. Remaining low-severity items are hardening for when wired to a real network boundary. The one medium finding (not yet wired) is a real architectural gap but out of this task's scope since no real backend integration point exists yet — tracked via follow-up task instead of blocking.
